excerpt: Safe Superintelligence (SSI) is Ilya Sutskever's AI lab with one stated goal: a safe superintelligence. Who runs it, what it has raised, its $32 billion valuation, and why it has no product.
content:
Safe Superintelligence Inc., or SSI, is an artificial intelligence research lab with a single stated aim. Its website calls it the world's first "straight-shot" superintelligence lab, with one goal and one product: a safe superintelligence. It says it treats safety and capabilities as technical problems to solve together, and that its business model keeps it away from short-term commercial pressure and product cycles.

SSI was founded in June 2024 by Ilya Sutskever, OpenAI's co-founder and former chief scientist, Daniel Gross, who previously led AI work at Apple, and Daniel Levy, a former OpenAI researcher. It describes itself as an American company with offices in Palo Alto and Tel Aviv.

Reports in 2025 said SSI raised $2 billion in April 2025 at a $32 billion valuation. CNBC reported that Meta tried to buy SSI earlier that year and was turned down. Gross then left at the end of June 2025 to join Meta, and Sutskever said on X that he would take over as chief executive, with Levy becoming president.

SSI has released no product or model, and sells nothing. There is no pricing to compare, and no public timeline for when, or whether, it will release anything. Its website holds a short mission statement, an updates page, job applications and contact details.

That makes SSI unusual among the best-funded AI labs: rivals such as OpenAI and Anthropic sell products to fund their research, while SSI has chosen not to.

This page is research, not a review: SSI has no product we could try. It brings together SSI's own website and the reporting linked under Sources, and says where each fact comes from.
